_doc: Rules read by slot_allocator.py (SLOT_ALLOCATOR_BUILD_RULES_FILE). Design: design/RimMandrake/operating_modes_2026-10-26.md §1.1-1.5 and §9 (the measured pacing). Every number here is a line from those sections; [A] marks a proposal the owner has not ruled, [O] one he ruled (with his words). Change a number here, not in the code.
_owner: [O] 2026-10-26 13:05 PDT, relayed by BENCH: 'If you already built the capability, please use it to determine the number of Foundry and Bench agents yourself. My 5 was a guess.' So no fixed cap: the allocator sets N per seat inside the budget.

split._doc: [A] FOUNDRY gets floor(total x share), BENCH the rest: total 4 -> BENCH 3 + FOUNDRY 1 (the 13:05 hand pick); total 1 -> BENCH only (ALMOST_OUT: FOUNDRY asleep, operating_modes §2.2).

_total_max: [A] operating_modes §3.1: more than about 10 at once never paid.

fallback_n._doc: used by the hook only when no allocation can be computed or read: the 13:05 hand baseline.

_burn_account: auto = the account whose latest MEASURED reading came from THIS machine's own live login (account_usage.py `machine`); name an account here to pin it.

CRUISE._steps: [A] used only when no burn rate is measured: P under 0.8 -> 2 total, under 1.0 -> 3, under 1.2 -> 4, else n.

token._session_brake: §1.5 rule 2: the burn account's 5-hour window above 90% used -> no new helpers until it resets

fit._msgs_per_pct: [A] the 13:05 hand calibration: 6 days of Lodestar usage_ledger.py message counts on the system account against its weekly %; used only while the account_usage series has too few points for a slope.
fit._doc: R8: total fit = mean helpers running over the window x (sustainable %/h = % left / hours to reset) / measured %/h. Raised by at most raise_step per 15-min check; lowered at once.

spare._doc: an account the seats do not burn, with no entry under lent_accounts, is named as a recommendation when it has this much left. Never switched automatically.

steven._owner: [O] 2026-10-27, owner ruling (ledger note on LIVE_FIXER_DESIGN_ONE_SEAT_NO_SHUTTLE, 7a3e09b63f): 'Dispatcher can use Steve up to 50% after a fresh reset only.' (narrows his 2026-10-26 rule: 'Steven uses his for other things ... We don't ever want to crowd him out.')
steven._max_used_by_us_pct: [O] 'up to 50%': at most 50% of his week used, all of it counted as ours (the meter cannot tell his use from ours; the side that never crowds him out).
steven._prefer_start_of_week_h: [O] 'after a fresh reset only'; the 48 h is [A] (the agent's reading of 'fresh reset'): we may draw only while at most 48 h have passed since his weekly reset (hours_to_reset >= 168-48); outside it the cap is 0. A hard limit.
steven._floor_pct_left: [A] safety floor: no plan may leave him under 10% of his week, ever.
steven._off_limits_through: [O] 'That has already happened this week, so we should simply leave Steve's account alone for now': off-limits until his weekly reset (account_usage week_resets_at 2026-10-28 15:00 PDT, read 2026-10-26 13:02). Set the next one only on his word.

presence._doc: [O] 'No, just adjust later to make up for any additional spend I incur.' Presence no longer lowers N; it only says whether he is in a window, which is when payback waits.

overage._doc: [O] 'adjust later to make up for any additional spend I incur'. Helper-hours above the computed N are owed; payback lowers N by ceil(owed / (hours to reset - finish_margin_h)), BENCH never under bench_floor. default_window_h applies when the reset is unknown. max_accrual_dt_h caps one interval so a gap in checks cannot invent hours.

helpers._doc: A helper is running when its transcript was written in the last live_window_s (over the 600 s silence kill) and its last assistant record is not a clean end_turn (no tool_use pending); a clean end_turn is finished at once. When in doubt, running.

ops._doc: What the allocator takes from ops_watch.py's status.json (V3_ROLES_BUILD_EIGHT_CHAIRS_ONE_TABLE). Only MEASURED points act (Codex runway also ESTIMATE). The disk brake caps the total before the owner's word, so his override still wins; Codex and the Steve lane are advice lines, because this allocator places Claude helpers, not Codex or testq work. A status older than stale_min is ignored and said so.
ops._disk_brake_free_gb: the DISK_LOW line in ops_watch_rules.json: one worst day of scratch growth (207 GB, 2026-10-26) left on the WSL volume
ops._disk_brake_total: one helper: enough to clear scratch or fix the cause, not enough to fill the disk
